title: QualityForge accessibility audit artifact v1
description: One accessibility audit of one page, produced by axe-core and shaped before it is written. It is not a defect artifact and carries no field of defect.v1: an audit exists whether or not anything failed, so binding the two would make every audit look like a defect.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this schema. A breaking change requires a new major.

url.description: Origin of the audited page, never a path, query or fragment: a query string is where a token would ride. A scheme with no origin, such as file:, is recorded as its scheme.

createdAt.description: When the audit ran, ISO-8601 in UTC.

engine.description: The analysis engine that produced the answer before it was shaped. Recorded because a rule's meaning belongs to its engine, not to this package.

counts.description: Summary numbers. nodes counts what was kept, not what the page produced — the difference is in totalNodes, per rule.

violations.description: Rules the engine decided were broken.

incomplete.description: Rules the engine could not decide. Kept apart from violations because it is not the same claim, and a consumer that merges them will report uncertainty as certainty.

rule.description: One rule and the nodes it matched.

id.description: The engine's rule identifier, such as color-contrast or label.

impact.description: How badly the rule is judged to matter. null means the engine did not say, and it is carried through as null: fail closed, so that 'we could not tell' never reads as 'it passed'.

nodes.description: The nodes kept for this rule, capped. How many were dropped is in totalNodes; a cap that does not say what it dropped is a silent loss.

totalNodes.description: How many nodes the rule really produced, before the cap. Never less than the number kept.

truncated.description: True when totalNodes exceeds the number of nodes kept.

target.description: Selectors the engine built to reach the element, kept whole and redacted. Without them, 48 nodes of one rule are indistinguishable, and where is half the message.

html.description: The element's structure only: tag name and attribute names, never an attribute value and never text. Measured across nine separate positions on a real page, node.html carried page content; the name of an attribute is never the secret, its value is.

failureSummary.description: The engine's own prose about the failure. Measured to carry no page content in any observation, which is why it survives whole while html does not.
